question: Among causal 20-60 session trajectories following trend-deterioration sentinels, what common characteristics distinguish known slow destructive bears from false-positive 50/200 EMA death-cross episodes?

design.negative_controls: Every 50/200 EMA false-positive episode in evaluable history, not a hand-selected subset.
design.sentinel_role: MA geometry is an anchor only; descriptor discovery is not restricted to 50/200 and may later support faster MA sentinels.
design.causality: Only observations available through each session; no future trough/recovery fields as predictors.

descriptor_families: return path geometry and drawdown velocity
failed rebound frequency/magnitude and lower-high/lower-low behavior
breadth level, slope, persistence, deterioration and failed recovery
realized volatility level, persistence and acceleration
VIX/VVIX level, persistence, term/trajectory where available
OFR funding/credit/volatility level, change and persistence with publication lag
moving-average geometry: distances, slopes, convergence/divergence and cross ordering
extreme down-day clustering and rebound asymmetry
discovery_method: Describe and rank effect separation between slow-crash windows and all false-positive windows. No single descriptor is assumed in advance. Sparse temporal combinations may be tested only after univariate/trajectory audit.
primary_metrics: direction consistency across both slow crashes
prohibited: post-hoc removal of difficult false positives
